trials.notes: Correct processor choice: WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for a flat document-order class edit. All HTML API calls are documented: next_tag, set_bookmark, seek, add_class, release_bookmark, get_updated_html. It follows the documented bookmark idiom for remembering the last matching tag, then uses add_class/get_updated_html correctly.

All HTML API methods used are documented, and the bookmark scan/edit pattern is sound. The main adherence loss is processor choice: it uses WP_HTML_Processor and always prefers create_full_parser based on method availability, even though the docs recommend the Tag Processor for flat position-based class edits and say create_full_parser is for complete documents. It also does not check get_last_error after an HTML Processor scan, so unsupported markup could be confused with no later H2.

Correctly uses WP_HTML_Tag_Processor with documented next_tag, set_bookmark, seek, add_class, release_bookmark, and get_updated_html. The implementation matches the documented last-match bookmark pattern. The only minor issue is an unnecessary class_exists guard outside the documented pattern; it is benign in this harness.

failure_analysis: All three trials passed all 6 hidden cases, so there are no failed hidden cases to attribute. The docs were effective in the relevant places: the Tag Processor 'Which processor should I use?' section directs flat position-based class edits to WP_HTML_Tag_Processor; next_tag documents case-insensitive tag matching and that tag-like text in comments is not matched; set_bookmark explicitly describes re-setting one bookmark to remember the last matching tag; add_class documents creating/appending class values; get_updated_html documents preserving untouched bytes. The main near-miss was trial-2: it passed, but its HTML Processor/full-parser fallback logic suggests the processor-choice and factory-choice warnings are still easy to miss.

doc_gaps.problem: The page demonstrates add_class with WP_HTML_Processor, which can make simple class edits look like an HTML Processor job even when no tree awareness is needed.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short decision note before the first example: use WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for flat document-order scans and attribute/class edits; use WP_HTML_Processor only when structure, breadcrumbs, subtree walking, parser errors, or normalized serialization matter.

doc_gaps.problem: A model selected create_full_parser whenever the method existed, rather than choosing based on whether the input contract was a complete document or a body fragment.
doc_gaps.suggestion: State explicitly that callers should not probe factories in sequence as a fallback strategy. Choose create_fragment for body fragments, create_full_parser only for complete start-to-finish documents, and prefer WP_HTML_Tag_Processor when mixed document-or-fragment input only needs lexical tag edits.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs mention unsupported-markup aborts, but the risk is separated from simple next_tag scanning examples. A passing implementation omitted get_last_error after using WP_HTML_Processor for a scan.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a post-scan reminder: after WP_HTML_Processor traversal, false can mean no match or parser abort; check get_last_error when the distinction affects whether to mutate, return unchanged, or fall back.
